text:
incident-bot: Pager: latency-steering-alert triggered for region-eu -> region-apac path. Symptoms: increased p95/p99 requests, elevated 502/504s for some customers, and spikes in cross-region tail latency. Auto-runbooks triggered.

alex-oncall: I’m on it. seeing spike at 22:04 UTC. Can someone verify if geo-steer probe jobs had a rollout in last 30m? @sam-netops? :eyes:

sam-netops: digging. I see a small policy change pushed ~21:58 by automation: weight adjustments for apac targets. Noted probe success rate dropped shortly after.

lara-eng: telemetry shows a sudden rise in retransmits on the eu-egress AS paths into apac, but only for requests hitting our steer policy variant v3. v2 looks stable.

alex-oncall: ok. hypothesis: v3 steering weight update + some CDN DNS cache retention created mixed pinning leading to asymmetric routing and high tail latency. Need to confirm with DNS traces.

tayla-telemetry: past 5m, trace sample:
```
trace_id: 0x7f32b
path: client -> cdn-edge1 -> eu-gw -> us-mid -> apac-ingress
latency: 1.2s tail
http_status: 502
```
not all traces show same path, some go eu -> apac directly and are fine.

sam-netops: run @alex a quick `dig` from our east-eu probe:
```
$ dig +short _route.example.com @1.1.1.1
apac-cname.example.net.
```
TTL still 300 in some caches. That would cause pinned clients to keep hitting apac despite new route weights.

alex-oncall: thanks. Action plan: 1) revert weight change for v3 to previous stable values (rollback). 2) temporarily disable latency-steering for eu region (force policy to latency-disabled) to stop oscillation. 3) instruct ops to issue a low TTL re-announce or change CNAME to force caches to refresh if rollback not enough. Who can push rollback?

lara-eng: I can push rollback to control-plane; preparing canary first. Pushing to canary now.

incident-bot: Deploy start: control-plane/steer-config v3 -> rollback-2025 by lara-eng at 22:09 UTC. CI checks passed.

alex-oncall: monitoring... canary looks good, success rate for canary traces back to baseline. Rolling to 10% then 100%.

lara-eng: rolled to 100% at 22:14 UTC.

sam-netops: disabling latency-steering flag for eu region now: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/flags/latency-steering?region=eu&state=off` -> 200 OK.

robin-pm: customer-impact note: managed customers on dedicated pools saw intermittent 502s for ~15-20m. Self-serve hosted users had p95 hit but not widespread errors. We should draft a brief post-incident note once stable.

alex-oncall: running synthetic checks: `curl -sv https://app.example.com/health --resolve app.example.com:443:eu-edge` shows steady 200s now. P99 dropped from 1.2s -> 210ms after rollback and flag off.

tayla-telemetry: adding graphs to incident timeline. p99 graph: spike starts 21:58, peaks 22:06, declines 22:09 after canary, normal by 22:18.

sam-netops: despite rollback some CDNs still return old cname due to TTLs. I’m coordinating with CDN partners to flush caches for critical prefixes. ETA 30m for full propagation.

alex-oncall: mitigation summary in thread: rollback steer weights -> stopped creating new mixed paths; disabled latency-steering -> prevented further automatic adjustments; CDN cache flush requested -> mitigates lingering pinned clients.

lara-eng: leaving a temp runbook note in ops: if steer rollout causes tail spike, immediate rollback + steering disable is recommended. Will create a PR to update runbook with TTL-drain step.

robin-pm: flagging for postmortem: we need guardrails around automated weight adjustments during CDN cache churn windows and better canary thresholds. Also an annotation in control-plane UI when TTLs are high.

alex-oncall: handing off to night team at 23:00 UTC. @sam-netops and @lara-eng — please keep watch on traces and CDN flush confirmation. If p99 rises above 500ms alert pager.

sam-netops: noted. I’ll watch network retransmits and confirm CDN flushes.

lara-eng: will monitor control-plane metrics and follow up with a short postmortem draft tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> customer errors reduced. Status: monitoring. Incident created: 5321004321.

alex-oncall: final note before handoff: impacted window ~21:58–22:18 UTC, most customers recovered by 22:18, limited lingering errors for pinned clients until CDN flushes complete.

robin-pm: drafting customer-facing blurb: short summary, what went wrong, immediate mitigations, next steps (runbook + UI guardrails). Will share in #product after postmortem. :memo:

sam-netops: CDN partner confirmed flush for the critical prefixes at 22:40 UTC. Logs show caches served new CNAMEs after that.

tayla-telemetry: last check 23:00 UTC: p99 stable at baseline, 502 rate back to normal. Marking incident as resolved in monitoring but keeping thread open for postmortem notes.

alex-oncall: thanks everyone. Handoff complete.
